# Raft Log Storage #

Dragonboat uses [Pebble](https://github.com/cockroachdb/pebble) to store Raft logs, it also supports RocksDB.

## Compatibility ##

Pebble is a new Key-Value store implemented in Go with bidirectional compatibility with RocksDB.

You can choose to use RocksDB for production purposes if that makes you more confortable. You can switch back to Pebble in the future any time you want. 

## Pebble ##

Pebble is used by default, no configuration is required.

## RocksDB ##

To use RocksDB as Dragonboat's storage engine, you need to install RocksDB first. You may also need to set the CGO_CFLAGS and CGO_LDFLAGS environmental variables to point to your RocksDB installation location when building your own applications.

Switch to RocksDB only involves one extra line of code, just set the LogDBFactory field of your config.NodeHostConfig to rocksdb.Factory available in the github.com/lni/dragonboat/v3/plugin/rocksdb.

## Use custom storage solution ##

You can extend Dragonboat to use your preferred storage solution to store Raft logs -

* implement the ILogDB interface defined in the github.com/lni/dragonboat/v3/raftio package
* pass a factory function that creates such a custom Log DB instance to the LogDBFactory field of your NodeHostConfig.Expert instance

item.text:
This pass converted the Finding 2 impact claim from reasoning into an executed observation, and captured the final audit matrix.

**New this pass**

- **Finding 2 impact boundary, executed** (`TestAuditDroppedReadIndexIsIdempotent`): feeding the same `SystemCtx` through `pendingReadIndex.dropped` twice leaves exactly one notification on the client channel — the second call is a no-op because the batch was already deleted. So the duplicated record does not double-complete a request today; the defect is the wrong raft update.
- **Finding 1 boundary, executed** (`TestAuditNodeUserReadIndexTwoTickTimeout`): a two-RTT timeout succeeds on the `INodeUser` path while one RTT fails, confirming the failure is precisely the one-tick dispatch delay.

**Final audit-tagged matrix**

```
root package:  PASS DroppedReadIndexIsIdempotent, LargeProposal, LargeProposalTwoNodes,
               LeaderTransfer, NodeUserReadIndexDispatchLatency, FollowerReadIndex,
               NodeUserReadIndexTwoTickTimeout, ObserverReadAndPropose
               FAIL NodeUserReadIndexOneTickTimeout                 (F1)
internal/raft: PASS RaftSafetyFuzz, InMemoryLogModel, CandidateProposalIsDroppedOnce,
               VoteSurvivesRestart
               FAIL CandidateReadIndexIsDroppedOnce, PeerUpdateDroppedReadIndexes (F2)
               FAIL UpdateHasUpdateWithDroppedReadIndexes           (F3)
```

All default suites remain green (including the transport suite with generated TLS certs in the diagnostic copy), and the implementation is byte-identical to `../source`.

**Findings**

- F1 — `(*nodeUser).ReadIndex` in [nodehost.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/nodehost.go:2063) never wakes the execution engine; ~one RTT latency and deterministic `RequestTimeout` for one-tick timeouts. Causality confirmed by a one-line fix in `audit/diag`.
- F2 — `handleCandidateReadIndex` in [raft.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/internal/raft/raft.go:1998) records a dropped ReadIndex twice; visible via `Peer.GetUpdate`, currently idempotent downstream.
- F3 — `pb.Update.HasUpdate` in [raftpb/raft.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/raftpb/raft.go:112) ignores `DroppedReadIndexes`, contradicting `Peer.HasUpdate` for the same state; no production caller.

[report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/report.md) carries the full write-up, reproduction inventory and command log. Remaining work is source-only review of rocksdb-backed code that cannot build offline.
